scout:
**SQANR Dispatch – Wed 4 Nov 2026, ~18:00 GMT**

**Lead: the midterms, oil and the Fed**

- **Democrats swept Congress and markets rallied.** 
The Dow rose about 2.8% (roughly 1,400 points) and the S&P 500 climbed 1.7%.
 
The S&P was set for its best session in three months, and a gauge of tech megacaps rallied 3% after a recent selloff.
 
The VIX fell about 15% to 17.62.

- **The risk to the S&P rally is data-center policy.** 
Markets are pricing the chance that ballot measures and newly elected officials restrict data center construction.
 That cuts against the AI and Nuclear parts of our thesis. 
Nvidia and Micron fell more than 1% on the news.
 
Apple and Microsoft each hit all-time highs.

- **Oil is falling on the Iran war politics.** 
The Democratic sweep highlighted opposition to the Iran war and extended this week's plunge in oil.
 
Brent fell below $100.
 Quotes vary by source and timestamp. 
One feed showed Brent at $94.39 at 17:31 UTC.
 
The conflict began in late February and sharply reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
 Energy names (XOM, CVX, COP, CNQ) are exposed if the decline continues. 
Energy's 12-month gain is still about 47%.

- **Treasuries and crypto.** 
Treasury yields dropped across the curve and the dollar slipped against all developed-world currencies.
 
Bitcoin topped $80,000.


**The Fed is hiking, not cutting**

- 
The Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% on 28 October, by a 10–2 vote.
 
The two dissenters wanted another quarter-point hike.
 
This follows a quarter-point increase at the 16 September meeting.

- 
The next decision is Wed 9 Dec at 2:00 PM EST. As of 3 Nov, OIS pricing implied a 77% chance of a 25bp hike.

- 
September CPI ran at 3.7% year on year, up from 3.4% in August.

- **CPI on Tue 10 Nov is the key print.** 
It is the last inflation reading before the 9 December decision.
 The oil drop should help the headline number, but it is not in that data yet.
- 
Chair Kevin Warsh has argued against sharing forward guidance.
 Don't expect hints from him.
- **Jobs data.** 
ADP showed private payrolls up 86,000 in October, above expectations.
 Friday's expected 63K nonfarm print (from the council calendar) looks beatable. A strong number would support the hike.
- **Other central banks.** 
The RBA has raised four times this year to 4.60%, and markets priced a fifth hike to 4.85% on 3 Nov.
 I could not confirm the outcome.

**Tech, AI and semis**

- **Chips are rebounding after a rough stretch.** 
In mid-October, 20 of the largest AI and semiconductor stocks lost more than $1 trillion in a week. The drivers were rate hikes, AI financing worries and competition.
 
On Tuesday nearly every chip and storage stock in the S&P 500 rose, led by memory and chip-equipment names.
 
Tom Sosnoff argues AMD, Nvidia and Micron "have not sold off enough."
 Intel is the exception. 
A report called its stock collapse "getting worse."

- **AMD beat.** 
Q3 adjusted EPS was $2.09 on revenue of $13.38B, and the stock was up 6.33% premarket.

- **Nvidia (NVDA) sits near $209.** 
It is prioritizing its highest-margin chips for OpenAI and Anthropic, and trades below its major short- and medium-term moving averages.
 
CNBC reports ByteDance is building AI chip capacity outside China using Nvidia Blackwell chips.
 Earnings are Tue 17 Nov after the close.
- **Palantir beat but the stock slipped.** 
Q3 EPS was $0.44 against $0.41 expected, and revenue was $2.31B against $2.18B.
 
U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time.
 
Shares lost 1.65% on Tuesday after analysts flagged a slowdown in total contract value.
 
U.S. commercial TCV was $1.5B, up 11% from last year.
 
Guidance for Q4 revenue is $2.649–2.653B, well above the $2.46B Wall Street expected.

- **Apple.** 
It beat Q4 estimates on strong iPhone sales but missed on China revenue.
 
Apple has also been reckoning with a global memory crunch.
 That crunch is good for MU, SNDK and the Korean memory names.
- **Disney.** 
A report says its theme parks, TV and movie units face deep cuts.
 Earnings are 17 Nov.
- **Anthropic IPO.** 
Robinhood is in a "food fight" for Anthropic IPO retail allocation.
 That is a sentiment marker for AI. I could not confirm the IPO date.
- **Movers today.** 
SHOP was up about 7%.
 
NVO beat Q3 estimates with EPS of $0.89 and was up about 5% premarket.


**Calendar, next two weeks** (dates from the council calendar unless noted)

- **Today (4 Nov):** ISM services is expected at 54.8. ARM, QCOM and MCK report after the close. CVS, MCD, NVO and UBER reported before the open. TM is also due. I did not confirm ARM or QCOM results. Both are chip and AI-adjacent, so check them first.
- **Thu 5 Nov:** CNQ, COP, PH and SONY report before the open. The energy names face a falling-oil backdrop.
- **Fri 6 Nov:** jobs report, expected 63K. BRK.B reports.
- **Tue 10 Nov:** CPI, 8:30 ET. PBR reports after the close.
- **Wed 11 Nov:** CSCO reports.
- **Thu 12 Nov:** AMAT reports after the close. It is a read on chip-equipment spending after Tuesday's equipment rally.
- **Fri 13 Nov:** PPI. The Japanese banks MUFG, MFG and SMFG report.
- **Tue 17 Nov:** retail sales. BHP, HD, MDT, PDD, DIS and NVDA (after the close) report. This is the heaviest day.
- **Wed 18 Nov:** 
FOMC minutes are due at 2:00 p.m. ET.
 LOW, TJX and PANW (after the close) report. Minutes could confirm how close the vote was to a hike.
- **Thu 19 Nov:** WMT reports.
- **Beyond the window:** BABA, ADI and DELL report 24 Nov. GDP and PCE are due 25 Nov.

**Sentiment and positioning**

- The reflex is relief. The VIX fell sharply, and money moved into both Treasuries and equities. Bitcoin is also bid.
- The AI trade is fragile. Funding costs and debt-heavy balance sheets drove the October rout. 
CoreWeave fell 15% in one session before Jensen Huang's comments steadied it.
 Rising hike odds and any data-center restrictions are the main threats.
- **Gaps:** I could not confirm fund-flow data, short interest or options positioning. I also could not confirm the Space, Quantum or Robotics headlines for this week.

redteam.statement: The council's real concentration is rate duration, not AI. SHY 18.5%, VZ 6.9%, PFE, CB, KO, PG, V are all bond proxies. VZ at an 11x P/E with a 20% FCF yield is priced for a dividend cut or share loss, and the book calls it value. A 10-year at 4.91% with a December hike 77% priced hits those multiples too. Second: the 'AI cluster is 12-16%' count leaves out GOOG, AMZN, MSFT and UBER's autonomy exposure. Third: eight seats own the same four names, so exits will be crowded. What is sound: SHY is real carry, and NVDA is sized for the Nov 17 print.

attacks.argument: 6.9% in the single largest equity line. A 20% FCF yield at 11x is a distress signal, not a bargain. Starlink Mobile with Qualcomm attacks pricing, and the stock is already up 7% on the week and crowded.
Hidden duration factor: VZ, PFE, CB, KO, PG, V, BRK-B and RSP all lose when the 10-year hits 5%. A hot CPI on Nov 10 hits these together. The 'diversified defensives' are one rate bet.
5.5% with eight seats behind it ahead of the Nov 17 print. Chinese customers face a 99% shortfall, data-center moratoria are spreading, and it sits below its 50-day. The trade is crowded and binary.
Down 28% from its high with RSI 23 and 'no clear cause in the filings'. A 0.5% FCF yield means capex absorbs the cash. Cheap at 15x P/E only if the earnings hold, and nobody can say why it fell.
Presented as the AI hedge, but it is $220B of AWS capex and growth that decelerated 7.5pp. It is the same financing trade with a retail label, so it belongs in the AI cluster count.
A 10.8x P/E on +379% growth is peak-cycle earnings. Beta is 3.25, CXMT is arriving, and the stock fell 17% in a week. Low P/E at a cyclical peak is a warning, not a margin of safety.
Equal-weight has a 2.2% 3-month lead and RSI 71. It owns the small and mid-cap names a hike hurts most, so it is not an AI hedge against rates.

cut.reason: Binary Nov 12 print after a 30% drop, in a cluster already counted. Lam showed cautious guidance.
Cap at 3-4%; crowded across eight seats, with Starlink pricing risk and no growth to underwrite the yield.
Peak-cycle earnings at beta 3.25; the same financing factor as NVDA with worse volatility.

blind_spots: Eight of eleven seats converged on the same names, so exit liquidity is the shared risk.
GOOG, AMZN and MSFT are counted outside the AI cluster, but all depend on data-center capex funding.
A hot CPI hurts SHY mark-to-market, the bond-proxy equities and the AI cluster on the same day.
Data-center policy risk is a political shock the council cannot price from this data.
redteam.killer_scenario: Hot CPI on Nov 10 pushes the 10-year above 5% and locks in a December hike. Bond proxies and RSP de-rate together, a light NVDA guide on Nov 17 hits the AI cluster, and no sleeve hedges both.

risk.statement: The largest risk is one rate factor hiding in many lines. A 10-year at 5% after a hot CPI on 10 Nov hits VZ, PFE, CB, KO, PG, V, BRK-B and RSP together, so I cap that bucket at 20% of capital. The second risk is the AI financing cluster: NVDA, MSFT, GOOG, AMZN and MU. I cap it at 22% with a 17 Nov binary print inside it. VZ is capped at 3%: a 20% FCF yield is a distress signal and Starlink Mobile threatens pricing. MU is vetoed as peak-cycle beta 3.25. AMAT is vetoed ahead of the 12 Nov print. Minimum cash 10% beyond SHY. I will not choke SHY; it is the carry.

vetoes.reason: Peak-cycle earnings, beta 3.25, CXMT supply risk; same financing factor as NVDA with worse volatility.
Binary 12 Nov print after a 30% monthly drop, inside an already crowded AI cluster.
Net margin -20%, down 48% in a month, worst day since 1974; no floor or dated catalyst.
Roughly $115B all-stock Lumentum deal dilutes holders; down 45% in a month; governance and financing risk.

concerns: Rate bucket (VZ, PFE, CB, KO, PG, V, BRK-B, RSP) must not exceed 20% combined; one hot CPI on 10 Nov hits all of it.
AI financing cluster (NVDA, MSFT, GOOG, AMZN, ANET) must not exceed 22%; NVDA reports 17 Nov after the close.
Eight seats hold the same names, so exits will be crowded; keep SHY and cash liquid for the CPI shock.
GOOG down 28% with no stated cause and 0.5% FCF yield; keep it small until the cause is explained.
UBER at 5% rests on one soft Q4 bookings guide and autonomy disruption risk; reassess after next print.

chairRaw.statement: The council will hold 41% in SHY and cash into the 10 November CPI print. The equity book stays inside every cap the risk manager set. Two arguments carried the ruling. First, the red team is right that the real concentration is rate duration, so I hold the rate bucket to 17%. Second, AI is still the core of our founding outlook, but it is a financing trade, so the cluster stops at 17% and NVDA at 4% into its 17 November print. The rest goes to earnings that do not depend on the 10-year: UBER, health care with its own catalysts, CB and a small XOM hedge. I overrule Forge's 46% in SHY because it is a refusal to judge. I also decline SPCX and the nuclear-power names: beta near 3 against a fresh data-center policy shock is not an edge.

events.text:
**SQANR Scout dispatch, Wed 4 Nov 2026, 18:00 GMT**

I ran one broad search and did not get to space, quantum, nuclear or robotics news or this week's earnings. Those gaps are marked below.

**Lead: the Fed's next move is a hike, and the data is split**
- 
September CPI was reported at 3.7%, with energy prices far above last year.

- 
September payrolls came in at just 29,000.
 That print is the labour-market counterweight to the inflation data.
- Wall Street's pricing, per one daily briefing, is that 
the Fed leans towards a hike.
 Yields rose on Tuesday. 
Wall Street ended mixed.
 The briefing's headline put the Nasdaq up 0.8%. I couldn't confirm the closing levels for the S&P 500 or the Dow.
- The next Fed meeting is 
9 December
. Friday's jobs report is the last big labour read before it. 
Friday's jobs report and next week's CPI will move that.

- Not confirmed: the current fed funds level and the exact December hike odds.

**Backdrop from recent weeks**
- The tape has swung on each jobs print this year. Hot data sank tech: 
the Nasdaq fell 4% on a hot May report as semiconductors plummeted amid rate-hike bets.
 Soft data lifted it: 
stocks jumped on 2 October after a weak September report, led by tech.

- On 2 October, 
the S&P 500 closed at 7,722.72 and the Nasdaq Composite at 27,190.86, an intraday record
. 
Nvidia led the Nasdaq to that record, and August payrolls were revised down to 133,000.
 That makes AI and semiconductors (NVDA, SMH, AVGO, TSM) the most rate-sensitive part of the SQANR book.
- Read-through: a hot Friday number with hot CPI on 10 November is the main downside risk for long-duration tech. A soft number helps tech but adds to stagflation worries.

**Next 48 hours**
- **Today, 4 Nov:** ISM services is expected at 54.8. After the close, ARM, QCOM and MCK report. ARM and QCOM are the key chip and AI read-throughs. Before the open, MCD, UBER, CVS, NVO and TM reported. I haven't confirmed their results.
- **Thu 5 Nov:**
  - 
The Bank of England decides on rates. US jobless claims are due, with a consensus of 195,000. Productivity is due, with a consensus of 2.5%. The Fed's Hammack and Barkin speak. Banxico decides on rates.

  - SONY, COP, CNQ and PH report earnings.
- **Fri 6 Nov:** The October jobs report is expected at about 63K. BRK.B reports.
- **Energy:** 
Crude stocks fell 1.9m barrels to 410.6m, gasoline stocks rose 3.9m and distillates fell 1.5m in the week to 23 October.
 That supports crude, and the energy-driven inflation story with it.

**Calendar, next two to three weeks (your list, with what matters most)**
- **10 Nov, CPI:** the decisive print for December hike odds. PBR reports after the close.
- **11 Nov:** CSCO reports.
- **12 Nov:** AMAT reports after the close, which is a read on chip equipment demand.
- **13 Nov:** PPI. MUFG, MFG and SMFG report.
- **17 Nov:** Retail sales. NVDA reports after the close and is the biggest single catalyst for the AI sleeve. HD, DIS, BHP, MDT and PDD also report.
- **18 Nov:** PANW reports after the close. LOW and TJX report before the open.
- **19 Nov:** WMT reports.
- **24 Nov:** DELL, BABA and ADI report.
- **25 Nov:** GDP, PCE and DE earnings.

**Not confirmed, and worth a follow-up before positioning**
- **Space, quantum, nuclear and robotics:** I found no catalysts. Check SPCX, PLTR, GEV, the quantum names and TSLA for company news.
- **Earnings reactions and guidance** for today's reporters (ARM, QCOM, UBER, MCD, NVO), plus any Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta or Amazon capex commentary from last week.
- **Geopolitics and energy:** I couldn't confirm what is driving the energy price spike.
- **Flows and positioning:** I found no data on fund flows, CFTC positioning or the VIX.

**SQANR Dispatch – Wed 4 Nov 2026, ~18:00 GMT**

**Lead: the midterms, oil and the Fed**

- **Democrats swept Congress and markets rallied.** 
The Dow rose about 2.8% (roughly 1,400 points) and the S&P 500 climbed 1.7%.
 
The S&P was set for its best session in three months, and a gauge of tech megacaps rallied 3% after a recent selloff.
 
The VIX fell about 15% to 17.62.

- **The risk to the S&P rally is data-center policy.** 
Markets are pricing the chance that ballot measures and newly elected officials restrict data center construction.
 That cuts against the AI and Nuclear parts of our thesis. 
Nvidia and Micron fell more than 1% on the news.
 
Apple and Microsoft each hit all-time highs.

- **Oil is falling on the Iran war politics.** 
The Democratic sweep highlighted opposition to the Iran war and extended this week's plunge in oil.
 
Brent fell below $100.
 Quotes vary by source and timestamp. 
One feed showed Brent at $94.39 at 17:31 UTC.
 
The conflict began in late February and sharply reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
 Energy names (XOM, CVX, COP, CNQ) are exposed if the decline continues. 
Energy's 12-month gain is still about 47%.

- **Treasuries and crypto.** 
Treasury yields dropped across the curve and the dollar slipped against all developed-world currencies.
 
Bitcoin topped $80,000.


**The Fed is hiking, not cutting**

- 
The Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% on 28 October, by a 10–2 vote.
 
The two dissenters wanted another quarter-point hike.
 
This follows a quarter-point increase at the 16 September meeting.

- 
The next decision is Wed 9 Dec at 2:00 PM EST. As of 3 Nov, OIS pricing implied a 77% chance of a 25bp hike.

- 
September CPI ran at 3.7% year on year, up from 3.4% in August.

- **CPI on Tue 10 Nov is the key print.** 
It is the last inflation reading before the 9 December decision.
 The oil drop should help the headline number, but it is not in that data yet.
- 
Chair Kevin Warsh has argued against sharing forward guidance.
 Don't expect hints from him.
- **Jobs data.** 
ADP showed private payrolls up 86,000 in October, above expectations.
 Friday's expected 63K nonfarm print (from the council calendar) looks beatable. A strong number would support the hike.
- **Other central banks.** 
The RBA has raised four times this year to 4.60%, and markets priced a fifth hike to 4.85% on 3 Nov.
 I could not confirm the outcome.

**Tech, AI and semis**

- **Chips are rebounding after a rough stretch.** 
In mid-October, 20 of the largest AI and semiconductor stocks lost more than $1 trillion in a week. The drivers were rate hikes, AI financing worries and competition.
 
On Tuesday nearly every chip and storage stock in the S&P 500 rose, led by memory and chip-equipment names.
 
Tom Sosnoff argues AMD, Nvidia and Micron "have not sold off enough."
 Intel is the exception. 
A report called its stock collapse "getting worse."

- **AMD beat.** 
Q3 adjusted EPS was $2.09 on revenue of $13.38B, and the stock was up 6.33% premarket.

- **Nvidia (NVDA) sits near $209.** 
It is prioritizing its highest-margin chips for OpenAI and Anthropic, and trades below its major short- and medium-term moving averages.
 
CNBC reports ByteDance is building AI chip capacity outside China using Nvidia Blackwell chips.
 Earnings are Tue 17 Nov after the close.
- **Palantir beat but the stock slipped.** 
Q3 EPS was $0.44 against $0.41 expected, and revenue was $2.31B against $2.18B.
 
U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time.
 
Shares lost 1.65% on Tuesday after analysts flagged a slowdown in total contract value.
 
U.S. commercial TCV was $1.5B, up 11% from last year.
 
Guidance for Q4 revenue is $2.649–2.653B, well above the $2.46B Wall Street expected.

- **Apple.** 
It beat Q4 estimates on strong iPhone sales but missed on China revenue.
 
Apple has also been reckoning with a global memory crunch.
 That crunch is good for MU, SNDK and the Korean memory names.
- **Disney.** 
A report says its theme parks, TV and movie units face deep cuts.
 Earnings are 17 Nov.
- **Anthropic IPO.** 
Robinhood is in a "food fight" for Anthropic IPO retail allocation.
 That is a sentiment marker for AI. I could not confirm the IPO date.
- **Movers today.** 
SHOP was up about 7%.
 
NVO beat Q3 estimates with EPS of $0.89 and was up about 5% premarket.


**Calendar, next two weeks** (dates from the council calendar unless noted)

- **Today (4 Nov):** ISM services is expected at 54.8. ARM, QCOM and MCK report after the close. CVS, MCD, NVO and UBER reported before the open. TM is also due. I did not confirm ARM or QCOM results. Both are chip and AI-adjacent, so check them first.
- **Thu 5 Nov:** CNQ, COP, PH and SONY report before the open. The energy names face a falling-oil backdrop.
- **Fri 6 Nov:** jobs report, expected 63K. BRK.B reports.
- **Tue 10 Nov:** CPI, 8:30 ET. PBR reports after the close.
- **Wed 11 Nov:** CSCO reports.
- **Thu 12 Nov:** AMAT reports after the close. It is a read on chip-equipment spending after Tuesday's equipment rally.
- **Fri 13 Nov:** PPI. The Japanese banks MUFG, MFG and SMFG report.
- **Tue 17 Nov:** retail sales. BHP, HD, MDT, PDD, DIS and NVDA (after the close) report. This is the heaviest day.
- **Wed 18 Nov:** 
FOMC minutes are due at 2:00 p.m. ET.
 LOW, TJX and PANW (after the close) report. Minutes could confirm how close the vote was to a hike.
- **Thu 19 Nov:** WMT reports.
- **Beyond the window:** BABA, ADI and DELL report 24 Nov. GDP and PCE are due 25 Nov.

**Sentiment and positioning**

- The reflex is relief. The VIX fell sharply, and money moved into both Treasuries and equities. Bitcoin is also bid.
- The AI trade is fragile. Funding costs and debt-heavy balance sheets drove the October rout. 
CoreWeave fell 15% in one session before Jensen Huang's comments steadied it.
 Rising hike odds and any data-center restrictions are the main threats.
- **Gaps:** I could not confirm fund-flow data, short interest or options positioning. I also could not confirm the Space, Quantum or Robotics headlines for this week.

data.statement: The regime is a hiking Fed meeting 3.7% inflation with the 10-year at 4.9%, and that permits owning equities only where cash flows are real and rates matter less. Because real yields are 2.6% and the market prices a 77% chance of a December hike, long duration and leveraged AI capex are the fragile corner. Credit spreads widening 0.67pp in three months says liquidity is thinning, so I hold 20% cash and favour health care, staples, insurers and energy as a hedge. The oil drop is a risk to energy, which I size small. A soft CPI on 10 Nov would lift me toward semis; a hot print would cut equities further. I may be early, as I tend to be.

WELL at 3% is trend-chasing a REIT at +9% in a week while the 10-year sits at 4.9% and December hike odds are 77%. What does your momentum model say about rate-sensitive longs when real yields are 2.6% and rising over three months?

You hold 5% LLY, 4% AMGN, 5% GILD and 3% MDT, about 17% health care, all bought after 20% monthly gains. What is the historical drawdown after a 1-month surge like that, and why is a drug-pricing policy shock from the new Congress not your stated exit?

You size NVDA at 6% and MU at 5%, yet WDC and AMAT too. If your washout thesis is right, why trim NVDA, with +106% growth and a Nov 17 catalyst, below GOOG, which has no dated catalyst?

data.statement: Atlas, your memory and compute exposure is the weakest part of the book, and it sits next to a macro thesis that says AI financing is the strain. Where the bottleneck is, you hold a token. Where it isn't, you hold the hyperscalers paying for it.

questions.question: You hold MSFT, GOOG and AMZN, 18% combined, as cash-generative quality. Their FCF yields are 1.5%, 0.5% and 5.8% against debt-funded capex. If financing strain is your regime, why are they the AI spenders you own instead of the AI suppliers?

MU at 4% is conviction 2 on a 10.8x P/E, but you call it peak-cycle risk. Is that earnings power or a mirage at the top of the memory cycle? What contract-price datapoint would make you cut it or double it?

AT&T at 27% FCF yield with elevated debt in a hiking Fed: what is net debt to EBITDA, how much matures in 2027, and what refinancing rate breaks the dividend? Why does a 3% position justify the funding from XOM?

data.statement: Scout, you call DIS a neglected thesis change, but it is up 15% in a month at RSI 73, 0.4% off its high. Who is left to buy? Your catalysts are dated. Several of your sizings look like consensus held in disguise.

questions.question: DIS is +9.6% this week and +14.8% this month, 0.4% off its high, with only 4.6% TTM growth. Where is the neglect? What print on 17 Nov makes this a buy rather than a sell-the-news?

VRTX at 4% rests on a povetacicept FDA decision with no date in the book. How is that a dated catalyst? Why not size it at zero until the date is confirmed?

data.statement: Nova, the thing that could hurt your portfolio most is one trade: AI capex fear. You hold about 40% in names that share it, with 18% cash as the only cushion. I'm asking what you do when they all fall together, and what that costs us.

questions.question: MU at 10.8x and SNDK at 7.6x rest on trailing earnings from +379% revenue growth. If contract prices merely flatten, what is normalized earnings, and what P/E are you actually paying? Why is a cycle peak a margin of safety?

Second, AI is still the core of our founding outlook, but it is a financing trade, so the cluster stops at 17% and NVDA at 4% into its 17 November print. The rest goes to earnings that do not depend on the 10-year: UBER, health care with its own catalysts, CB and a small XOM hedge. I overrule Forge's 46% in SHY because it is a refusal to judge. I also decline SPCX and the nuclear-power names: beta near 3 against a fresh data-center policy shock is not an edge.
data.summary: Carry first: SHY at 4.59% plus cash covers a hot CPI and a December hike. AI exposure is held at quality and fair prices (MSFT, NVDA, GOOG, AMZN, ANET) and capped at 17%. Rate-proxy defensives are limited to 17%, and the balance sits in company-specific earnings in health care, mobility and insurance.

holdings.thesis: The 2-year pays 4.59% at 2% volatility while a December hike is 77% priced. It is the only sleeve that gains carry through a hot CPI, and it is dry powder after the 17 November NVDA print.
holdings.rotate_if: Soft CPI plus tighter credit spreads and a confirmed broad rally; redeploy into equities.

holdings.rotate_if: Q4 bookings come in below the soft guide, or a close below $64.

data.changes: This is the first portfolio, built from $100,000 in cash. The council enters with 41% in SHY and cash, a 17% AI cluster and a 17% rate-proxy bucket, all within the risk manager's caps. MU, AMAT, INTC and MRVL are excluded per the vetoes. KO and PG are left out to keep the rate bucket under its cap.

dissent.view: Wanted 46% in SHY. Overruled: that abandons judgment, and 41% in SHY plus cash already covers the CPI shock.
Wanted RSP at 14%. Overruled by the 5% cap; equal weight carries the hike-sensitive mid caps.
Wanted NVDA 6%, MSFT 8% and a MU starter. Overruled by the NVDA and MSFT caps and the MU veto.
Wanted CVX and NEM as real-asset hedges. One energy hedge, XOM, is enough, and gold is breaking support.
Wanted momentum names TXN, MA, LLY and AMGN. Overruled: they trade at RSI 71-77 exhaustion, with TXN inside the semiconductor drawdown.
Wanted 1% AMAT into the 12 November print. Vetoed by the risk manager; a binary print in a crowded cluster.

watch: 10 November CPI: a monthly print of 0.3% or more with the 10-year above 5% triggers more SHY; a soft print allows adding to NVDA and RSP.
NVDA earnings on 17 November after the close: the guide and China and data-center commentary.
AMAT on 12 November and ARM and QCOM results tonight, as reads on AI capex and Starlink handsets.
Data-center restrictions spreading beyond Texas; this is the main threat to the AGI and nuclear sleeves.
High-yield spreads above 3.6pp would signal broadening credit stress.
